MRVL.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers the news that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA, announced shortly before Monday's open. Shares of NVIDIA are up 31%. The Nasdaq (Nasdaq: QQQ) is up about 5.7%, the S&P 500 about 4% and the Dow Jones 2.1%. The VanEck semiconductor ETF (Nasdaq: SMH) is up 13%. Bleeker names three stocks with the most to gain outside NVIDIA. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell hard after big gains at the start of 2026, and Huang himself has said it could be the next trillion dollar company. It's rising along with the broader optics group after its recent move for Lumentum. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 14%, recovering Friday's losses, and Huang's return supports confidence in ecosystems like NeoClouds. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) is up 19% in a broad rebound of behind-the-meter power stocks that the elections had beaten down. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and many hyperscalers, which could have gained from losing a key rival, are seeing much more muted moves. Many of these stocks are up 15% or 20% but are mostly replacing losses from Friday and sometimes Thursday. Rising rates and the midterm elections remain as overhangs, and many chip stocks sit more than 50% below recent highs. Bleeker's question is whether this becomes an enduring rally.

LITE.headline: Semiconductor Stocks like Micron, Marvell, and Bloom Energy See Massive Gains as Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDIA
LITE.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers the news that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA, announced shortly before Monday's open. Shares of NVIDIA are up 31%. The Nasdaq (Nasdaq: QQQ) is up about 5.7%, the S&P 500 about 4% and the Dow Jones 2.1%. The VanEck semiconductor ETF (Nasdaq: SMH) is up 13%. Bleeker names three stocks with the most to gain outside NVIDIA. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell hard after big gains at the start of 2026, and Huang himself has said it could be the next trillion dollar company. It's rising along with the broader optics group after its recent move for Lumentum. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 14%, recovering Friday's losses, and Huang's return supports confidence in ecosystems like NeoClouds. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) is up 19% in a broad rebound of behind-the-meter power stocks that the elections had beaten down. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and many hyperscalers, which could have gained from losing a key rival, are seeing much more muted moves. Many of these stocks are up 15% or 20% but are mostly replacing losses from Friday and sometimes Thursday. Rising rates and the midterm elections remain as overhangs, and many chip stocks sit more than 50% below recent highs. Bleeker's question is whether this becomes an enduring rally.

Leading ETFs showed software up closer to 4% and semiconductors up 13%. Bleeker also pointed to two company-specific items. The New York Times reported that Anthropic's demand is so large that SpaceX needs new data centers by October to fill its orders. On Friday, Oracle said it has secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract. Bleeker notes Nvidia helped build neoclouds with funding, technical expertise and chips. He calls it a one-day win. Nebius is down 38% over the past month, CoreWeave 12% and Oracle 10%. Over six months Nebius is down more than 50%, Oracle 40% and CoreWeave 55%. Bleeker names three drivers of the selloff: higher rates and wider credit default swaps, political worries after the midterms, and Huang's removal. Only the last has reversed. Going forward, watch the Fed's rate path and how politics affects project locations such as Texas.

WULF.headline: Nebius & CoreWeave Jump 21% While Oracle Sees 12% Gains on Monday Following Jensen’s Return
WULF.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says neocloud stocks rallied Monday on the return of Jensen Huang to NVIDIA. At 1:30 p.m. Eastern, Nebius Group (NASDAQ: NBIS) and CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV) were each up 21%, IREN (NASDAQ: IREN) was up 25%, TeraWulf (NASDAQ: WULF) was up 13% and Oracle (NYSE: ORCL) was up 12%. Leading ETFs showed software up closer to 4% and semiconductors up 13%. Bleeker also pointed to two company-specific items. The New York Times reported that Anthropic's demand is so large that SpaceX needs new data centers by October to fill its orders. On Friday, Oracle said it has secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract. Bleeker notes Nvidia helped build neoclouds with funding, technical expertise and chips. He calls it a one-day win. Nebius is down 38% over the past month, CoreWeave 12% and Oracle 10%. Over six months Nebius is down more than 50%, Oracle 40% and CoreWeave 55%. Bleeker names three drivers of the selloff: higher rates and wider credit default swaps, political worries after the midterms, and Huang's removal. Only the last has reversed. Going forward, watch the Fed's rate path and how politics affects project locations such as Texas.

BE.headline: Semiconductor Stocks like Micron, Marvell, and Bloom Energy See Massive Gains as Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDIA
BE.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers the news that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA, announced shortly before Monday's open. Shares of NVIDIA are up 31%. The Nasdaq (Nasdaq: QQQ) is up about 5.7%, the S&P 500 about 4% and the Dow Jones 2.1%. The VanEck semiconductor ETF (Nasdaq: SMH) is up 13%. Bleeker names three stocks with the most to gain outside NVIDIA. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell hard after big gains at the start of 2026, and Huang himself has said it could be the next trillion dollar company. It's rising along with the broader optics group after its recent move for Lumentum. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 14%, recovering Friday's losses, and Huang's return supports confidence in ecosystems like NeoClouds. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) is up 19% in a broad rebound of behind-the-meter power stocks that the elections had beaten down. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and many hyperscalers, which could have gained from losing a key rival, are seeing much more muted moves. Many of these stocks are up 15% or 20% but are mostly replacing losses from Friday and sometimes Thursday. Rising rates and the midterm elections remain as overhangs, and many chip stocks sit more than 50% below recent highs. Bleeker's question is whether this becomes an enduring rally.

NOW.headline: Palantir Rips 10% to Lead Software Stocks. Cloudflare and ServiceNow Also Join ‘Jensen Rally’
NOW.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA is lifting technology stocks on Monday. The NASDAQ was up more than 7% as of 1:30 p.m. Eastern, after opening with a 3% pre-market gain following Friday's sell-off. Chip stocks as a group rose more than 13%. Software is also higher, but the gains are uneven. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) are each up about 3%, while the IGV software ETF is up 4%. The biggest winners are companies that benefit from sovereign AI and a strong open-weight ecosystem. Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) leads at 10%, and Palantir has been one of the loudest backers of sovereign AI. Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.

CRWD.headline: CrowdStrike Shares Fall 10% After a $44 Billion Zscaler Deal Despite an Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance
CRWD.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., explains why shares of CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 10% on Monday, November 23, while most tech stocks rallied. The trigger was a proposed acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) for about $44 billion, announced the same morning. The sell-off came despite a strong report. CrowdStrike posted revenue growth of 28.3% against expectations of 23.9%, and EPS of $0.34 against $0.31. It also raised full-year guidance. Bleeker points to the deal instead: Zscaler's wide product line may be hard to integrate into CrowdStrike's platform, and the roughly 34% premium arrives when cybersecurity stocks are richly valued. Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs. Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.

ZS.headline: CrowdStrike Shares Fall 10% After a $44 Billion Zscaler Deal Despite an Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance
ZS.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., explains why shares of CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 10% on Monday, November 23, while most tech stocks rallied. The trigger was a proposed acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) for about $44 billion, announced the same morning. The sell-off came despite a strong report. CrowdStrike posted revenue growth of 28.3% against expectations of 23.9%, and EPS of $0.34 against $0.31. It also raised full-year guidance. Bleeker points to the deal instead: Zscaler's wide product line may be hard to integrate into CrowdStrike's platform, and the roughly 34% premium arrives when cybersecurity stocks are richly valued. Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs. Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.

NET.headline: Palantir Rips 10% to Lead Software Stocks. Cloudflare and ServiceNow Also Join ‘Jensen Rally’
NET.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., says Jensen Huang's return to NVIDIA is lifting technology stocks on Monday. The NASDAQ was up more than 7% as of 1:30 p.m. Eastern, after opening with a 3% pre-market gain following Friday's sell-off. Chip stocks as a group rose more than 13%. Software is also higher, but the gains are uneven. Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT) and Salesforce (NYSE: CRM) are each up about 3%, while the IGV software ETF is up 4%. The biggest winners are companies that benefit from sovereign AI and a strong open-weight ecosystem. Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) leads at 10%, and Palantir has been one of the loudest backers of sovereign AI. Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.

AAPL.headline: CrowdStrike Shares Fall 10% After a $44 Billion Zscaler Deal Despite an Earnings Beat and Raised Guidance
AAPL.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., explains why shares of CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 10% on Monday, November 23, while most tech stocks rallied. The trigger was a proposed acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS) for about $44 billion, announced the same morning. The sell-off came despite a strong report. CrowdStrike posted revenue growth of 28.3% against expectations of 23.9%, and EPS of $0.34 against $0.31. It also raised full-year guidance. Bleeker points to the deal instead: Zscaler's wide product line may be hard to integrate into CrowdStrike's platform, and the roughly 34% premium arrives when cybersecurity stocks are richly valued. Zscaler shares rose about 16%, while CrowdStrike is now down 26% from its recent highs. Bleeker lays out both cases. The bull case is that cybersecurity budgets must rise as companies patch systems, with outages at Apple and others as examples. The bear case is that frontier AI models may become the center of cyber defense, which raises questions about what companies like CrowdStrike offer. Expect choppy trading in these shares while investors sort that out.

Including his five takeaways on what the reversal says about corporate governance, the role Washington played in the decision, and the rally that's lifting the whole AI trade while sending AMD lower. Brian is joined by New Street Research technology infrastructure analyst Antoine Chkaiban on the new checks around Huang and why he's still a buyer; "In the Loop" host Ejaz on key-man risk and whether the "Bank of Nvidia" reopens for neoclouds; EMJ Capital founder and president Eric Jackson, who calls the return a win for open-source AI; Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman on the board's credibility and Colette Kress's future; Moor Insights & Strategy founder and chief analyst Patrick Moorhead on the politics behind the ouster and why nothing changes for AMD for 18 months; and SlateStone Wealth partner and chief market strategist Kenny Polcari on whether this kicks off a year-end rally.

Bleeker focuses on stocks lagging a market where nearly everything is up. Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) gained only about 1.7%, and he says a rotation back into AI-adjacent names could pull capital out of the safe-haven stock. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) rose about 6% at the open, trailing the NASDAQ and semiconductor indexes. It fell about 12% Friday on reports that Google was cutting some of its TPU allocation. Anthropic (NASDAQ: ANT) also rose 6%, but its shares have been under pressure since Thursday's IPO, and NVIDIA's backing of open-weight models is a competitive threat. CrowdStrike (NASDAQ: CRWD) fell about 5% at the open, partly on its $44 billion acquisition of Zscaler (NASDAQ: ZS). Bleeker notes that money that moved into cybersecurity as semiconductors sold off could rotate back. He says to watch for competitive pressure on these names in the coming weeks.

The biggest winners are companies that benefit from sovereign AI and a strong open-weight ecosystem. Palantir (NASDAQ: PLTR) leads at 10%, and Palantir has been one of the loudest backers of sovereign AI. Cloudflare (NYSE: NET) is up roughly 7%, and ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW) is up 5%, helped by its control tower software that guides customers between models and agentic workloads. Anthropic is lagging, since Huang has pushed open-weight models that pressure leading labs like Anthropic and OpenAI. Bleeker's takeaway: if Huang keeps backing open weight model makers, Palantir, Cloudflare and ServiceNow, up 5% to 10%, should keep outperforming the 2% to 3% gains in the rest of software.

On Friday, Oracle said it has secured all funding needed for its OpenAI contract. Bleeker notes Nvidia helped build neoclouds with funding, technical expertise and chips. He calls it a one-day win. Nebius is down 38% over the past month, CoreWeave 12% and Oracle 10%. Over six months Nebius is down more than 50%, Oracle 40% and CoreWeave 55%. Bleeker names three drivers of the selloff: higher rates and wider credit default swaps, political worries after the midterms, and Huang's removal. Only the last has reversed. Going forward, watch the Fed's rate path and how politics affects project locations such as Texas.

SPY.headline: Stocks Roar as the S&P 500 Jumps About 4.5% on News Jensen Huang Is Returning as NVIDIA CEO
SPY.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers a broad Monday rally led by chip stocks. The S&P 500 was up about 4.5% in midday trading, after news broke that Jensen Huang will return as CEO of NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA). The IT sector gained 8.6%, while financials rose 1.7%, utilities 0.96% and health care 0.9%. Real estate and energy declined. The State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA: SPY) rose about 4.5%. Chips drove the move. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (NASDAQ: SOXX) gained 12.9%, led by NVIDIA, which was up more than 30%. The iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (Cboe: IGV) rose about 4%, so software stocks reacted far less than chip stocks. The GraniteShares 2x Long NVIDIA Daily ETF (NASDAQ: NVDL) jumped 60% but is still down nearly 50% over the past month. NVIDIA traded around $180 before Huang's ouster and hasn't recovered that level. Many stocks bouncing 20% or more today fell 20% or more at the end of last week. Watch whether this is a relief rally or the start of a recovery after the market rotated out of AI and into defensive sectors.

QQQ.headline: Christmas Came Early For AI: Jensen Huang Is Back
Semiconductor Stocks like Micron, Marvell, and Bloom Energy See Massive Gains as Jensen Huang Returns to NVIDIA
QQQ.summary: Eric Bleeker, Chief Investment Officer at 24/7 Wall St., covers the news that Jensen Huang is returning to NVIDIA, announced shortly before Monday's open. Shares of NVIDIA are up 31%. The Nasdaq (Nasdaq: QQQ) is up about 5.7%, the S&P 500 about 4% and the Dow Jones 2.1%. The VanEck semiconductor ETF (Nasdaq: SMH) is up 13%. Bleeker names three stocks with the most to gain outside NVIDIA. Marvell Technology (NASDAQ: MRVL) fell hard after big gains at the start of 2026, and Huang himself has said it could be the next trillion dollar company. It's rising along with the broader optics group after its recent move for Lumentum. Micron Technology (NASDAQ: MU) is up 14%, recovering Friday's losses, and Huang's return supports confidence in ecosystems like NeoClouds. Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE) is up 19% in a broad rebound of behind-the-meter power stocks that the elections had beaten down. Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) and many hyperscalers, which could have gained from losing a key rival, are seeing much more muted moves. Many of these stocks are up 15% or 20% but are mostly replacing losses from Friday and sometimes Thursday. Rising rates and the midterm elections remain as overhangs, and many chip stocks sit more than 50% below recent highs. Bleeker's question is whether this becomes an enduring rally.
